title: Link two GPUs with the NVLink bridge that fits their slot spacing
instruction: Link the two GPUs with the NVLink bridge that fits them, and leave the other bridge on the mat. Finish with both arms back where they started.
context: Pairs of 48 GB RTX A6000 GPUs joined by an NVLink bridge (96 GB of GPU memory, 112.5 GB/s between them) are a standard build for labs and small teams that train and run models too big for one card, and the A40 data-centre card takes the same kind of bridge. Every such build, upgrade or repair ends with the bridge pushed onto both cards' NVLink connectors; NVIDIA's guide: connect the bridge into the labeled NVLink ports on the two GPUs. The hard part is physical: one part has to go onto two connectors 61 mm apart at once, and both ends have to be pushed home together and evenly, since each socket takes a firm push and a bridge cocked 4 degrees on its fingers levers the contacts. First the right bridge has to be taken: only the one whose socket spacing matches the cards' slot spacing can link them. A robot that does this reliably takes over a manual step in building AI compute.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A blue vinyl antistatic mat 2 mm thick from 5 to 52 cm forward and from 33 cm right to 24 cm left of the centre line. (2) On it, a Streacom BC1 V2 open benchtable: a 36 x 27 cm aluminium plate on four short legs carrying an ATX workstation motherboard (24.4 x 30.5 cm, from 8.9 to 33.3 cm forward, 16 cm right to 14.5 cm left) on standoffs, its top 2.9 cm above the table, with a CPU and top-flow cooler, four memory modules, and seven PCI Express x16 slots running forward, 20.32 mm apart, slot 1 at 3.05 cm left of the centre line and the rest toward the right; the bench's bracket bar along the board's far edge; its ATX power supply (steel box, 15 x 14 x 8.6 cm) stands on the mat behind it, at the left. All fixed. (3) Two NVIDIA RTX A6000 graphics cards (dual-slot, 267 x 111 mm, black aluminium and plastic shrouds), standing in slots 1 and 4, three slot pitches (60.96 mm) apart, with their cooler sides to the right and a 24 mm air gap between them; they run from 6.4 to 33.1 cm forward, their brackets screwed to the rail at the far end, their north (top) edges 14 cm above the table. Fixed. Each card's NVLink connector cover has been taken off: its gold NVLink fingers sit in a 47 x 9 mm cut-out in the shroud, 11 mm deep, centred 28.5 cm forward (4.6 cm from the bracket), on the card's circuit board line. The two black plastic covers lie on the mat at 12 cm forward, 21.5 and 25.5 cm right. (4) The two NVIDIA RTX A-series NVLink bridges, lying on their sockets on the mat with their long sides across (left-right): the 3-slot bridge (60.96 mm between its sockets; 68 x 48 x 11.2 mm, 36 g) centred 30 cm forward, 25.5 cm right, and the 2-slot bridge (40.64 mm; 47.6 x 48 x 11.2 mm, 29 g) centred 19 cm forward, 25.5 cm right. Each is a glossy black plastic cover on a circuit board over two grey plastic socket housings, 7 x 44 mm and 8 mm deep, one under each end, that go down over a card's fingers. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Each socket rests on its card's fingers at their lead-in and slides 6 mm down over them, to seated, only while it is pushed harder than 18 N; it stays where it is left. A bridge cocked 5 degrees binds: its lower end goes no further. Latched for the rest of the trial: 0.0 once either bridge has been cocked 4 degrees or more (one end of the 3-slot bridge 4.3 mm lower than the other) while one of its sockets is pushed onto a card's fingers (its contacts pried), or has fallen onto the motherboard. Otherwise judged at the end of the trial, on live states: 1.0: the 3-slot bridge seated on both cards (both sockets within 0.5 mm of fully down, level within 1 degree), the 2-slot bridge left on the mat all along (never moved 3 cm or lifted 2 cm) and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.75: the same with an arm not back; 0.5: the 3-slot bridge seated on both cards; 0.25: the 3-slot bridge sitting square in both connectors' cut-outs (level within 3 degrees), not yet pushed down; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with both bridges still. In a real trial: seated means no gap between either socket and its card's connector (a close photo at each end) and both ends at the same height above the cards (calipers, within 0.5 mm). Powering the bench and running nvidia-smi nvlink -s is an optional extra check, not needed for the score, so unpowered or non-working cards can be used. Pried means a side video shows one end 4 mm or more lower than the other while the bridge is on the fingers. The 2-slot bridge must not have been moved; the arms are checked against marks at their start.
reset_notes: Pull the bridge off the cards (if fitted) and lay both bridges back on the mat in their places, long sides across, 3-slot one further forward.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz). Real sizes; bridge masses 29 g (listed) and 36 g (computed by size). Each socket's push-on is a hidden sprung stop under it that gives way at 18 N and holds where left (design value), binding at 5 degrees (computed from the socket's play); the gold fingers are drawn, not collided; bench, board and cards are fixed. Cameras 1280x704 (Dream-1: 320x176).
